text:
maria: quick heads-up, nightly eval (doc-qna-small) regressed on generation quality — EM down ~12% vs baseline, started at 03:10 UTC.
akash: any config changes in the eval runner or sampler?
jon: i pushed a small RNG serialization fix to runtime yesterday afternoon, commit 0a1b2c. could be related to seed/state across warm starts :eyes:
maria: timeline lines up. i pulled the eval artifacts and there are subtle sampling diffs — same prompt, different tokens frequently.
akash: show diff if you have it?
maria: pasted quick config diff from the job config:
```
- sampling:
-   temp: 0.7
-   top_p: 0.95
-   seed: 42
+ sampling:
+   temp: 0.9
+   top_p: 0.92
+   # seed unset in this run (inherited runtime behavior)
```
evan: if seed is unset and RNG state persists differently between warm and cold starts, outputs will drift even with same model/quant.
ci-bot: deploy: redwood/runtime @0a1b2c deployed to staging at 2024-06-18T22:45:10Z (pipeline #7823) :white_check_mark:
akash: can we reproduce locally? run the nightly eval script with/without the runtime patch and compare token sequences.
maria: i ran a minimal repro with model-xyz-q8 on a single prompt. below are token sequences at step 1..8 (truncated):
- baseline (seed=42): [512, 23, 77, 9, 401, 12, 8, 99]
- current (seed unset): [512, 23, 77, 11, 400, 12, 8, 101]
evan: those differences at token 4 are exactly the kind that flip EM.
jon: the rng-serialize change ensured we persist RNG state across checkpoints to avoid reusing the same subsequence after restore. could have changed initial offset for continuous-batching warmups.
akash: hypothesis: after runtime change, when a warmed worker serves the eval, the KV-cache/warmup uses a different rng offset; if seed unset, different starting state -> sampling drift.
maria: actionable: 1) run a bisect across the last 5 deploys to confirm 0a1b2c correlation, 2) pin seed in nightly eval runner as a quick mitigant, 3) add a unit test for deterministic sampling across warm restarts.
evan: i can run a focused bisect on staging tomorrow morning — reproduce with same batch-size and quant flags.
jon: if bisect points to runtime change, we should either revert or add explicit RNG resync for determinism in eval mode. production users still want RNG continuity though.
akash: for the short term i'll add seed=42 to the nightly eval job and re-run to restore baselines. also adding a note in the deploy checklist to flag RNG-impacting changes.
maria: thanks — re-run queued. i'll attach eval artifacts and a minimal script to reproduce once evan has the bisect results. :thumbsup:
ci-bot: nightly-eval job 98451 queued with sampling.seed=42 at 2024-06-19T03:25:00Z
jon: filing a small postmortem checklist item to capture deterministic-eval requirements.
maria: adding me/akash/jon/evan to the follow-up. will update this thread with artifacts.
akash: TL;DR — likely seed/state alignment bug introduced by rng-serialize change; pin seed for nightly, bisect to confirm, then fix runtime semantics or add eval-only resync. :mag:
maria: good plan. thanks all.
